verdictMeaning: Independent approval of the repaired block10 explanation only, composed with D184's twenty unchanged SCI/ZH/EN passes. This is not figure, whole-course, source-pixel, native-stage, display, product-acceptance or handoff approval.

independence.previousReviewReadScope: Verdict metadata and D184-F01 only; no unaffected block assessments or prose were re-reviewed.

coverage.mechanicalDeltaEvidence: Reuse the already verified after-baseline delta: only /prose/9/text changed in each language; all formulas, source references, metadata, twenty unaffected blocks, section-break anchors, figures and tasks are unchanged. No full delta or native check was replayed.

affectedFindingDisposition.reason: Both repaired texts explicitly switch the alpha in the linear-time equation to continuously accumulated rotational phase, distinguish it from the principal normal-field angle, and explain equal cosines under the specified aligned-start rotation model.

modelConditions.assessment: Both languages state that the normal rotates in a plane containing the magnetic-field direction and that time zero is when the normal points along the field. Together with the retained uniform field, fixed area and uniform angular speed, these conditions support the source's full-amplitude cosine flux.

phaseVersusPrincipalAngle.assessment: The quantity that increases uniformly is explicitly the angle continuously accumulated from the aligned position, or rotational phase. The ordinary geometric angle is separately bounded between zero and half a turn. The explanation therefore does not assert indefinite increase of the principal angle.

cosineAndFluxEquivalence.assessment: The selected normal remains the same physical normal used in block8's signed-flux definition. Folding continuous phase to the principal normal-field angle preserves its cosine. At three quarters of a turn the principal angle is a quarter turn and both cosines are zero; after a full turn the principal angle is zero and both cosines are positive one. The block10 convention therefore connects correctly to block8's flux definition and block11's cosine time dependence.

originalFormulaAndNotation.assessment: The local source expressions for flux, linear rotation phase and cosine time dependence remain present unchanged. The repair clarifies the prose convention, not the equations. No new math, notation or source correction is requested.

frequencyMeaning.assessment: Both languages retain that the magnitude of rotational angular velocity equals the angular frequency of flux oscillation in this model, give radians per second, and distinguish ordinary frequency in cycles per second using the twice-pi conversion.

zhCompletenessAndNaturalness.assessment: The Chinese sequence supplies the geometry and time origin, names the continuously accumulated rotation angle and phase, contrasts it with the ordinary geometric angle, explains cosine equivalence, then gives the time relation and frequency meaning. The half-turn bound is understandable without introducing new notation; the transition to the retained flux law is coherent. No omission, mistranslation or actionable unnaturalness remains.

enCompletenessAndNaturalness.assessment: The English carries the same complete explanation, explicitly naming rotational phase and principal geometric angle. The aligned initial position, rotation plane, equal-cosine link, linear time law and frequency distinction form a clear technical sequence. The wording is natural and does not overgeneralize to arbitrary rotation geometry.

bilingualParity.assessment: The two languages agree on all affected scientific qualifications. Neither removes the source's physical result or makes a different angle, phase or flux claim.

freezePolicy: review-freeze.json binds the actual input, source baseline, inherited evidence, current bilingual outputs and this report. Any change to an affected input or reviewed output invalidates this affected approval; unchanged passed stages are reused.
